city_center.name: Downtown Asheville + Hendersonville Apple Country
city_center.landmark: Downtown Asheville's Art Deco core (Grove Arcade, City Building) in the Blue Ridge Mountains; Hendersonville orchards to the south
city_center.notes: Blue Ridge mountain town with a nationally strong local-food and brewery scene. Ingles Markets (headquartered in nearby Black Mountain, NC) is the home grocer. Hendersonville is one of the top apple-producing counties in the US. sources: amazingasheville.net architecture; romanticasheville.com apple country; Ingles HQ.

featured_frontier.signature_ingredient: Hendersonville apples (Aug-Feb, peak fall) + Appalachian sorghum and local honey

cultural_notes: Asheville is a Blue Ridge Mountains city where Appalachian tradition meets a nationally recognized local-food, brewery, and arts scene (source: asheville.com; mahec.net about-the-area)
Downtown Asheville holds one of the largest concentrations of Art Deco architecture in the South, second only to Miami Beach (source: amazingasheville.net; grayline.com Asheville architecture)

Hendersonville, just south of Asheville, is nationally known as Apple Country -- one of the top apple-producing counties in the US -- and apples run August through February in North Carolina (source: romanticasheville.com Hard Apple Cidery Trail; buncombe.ces.ncsu.edu NC Cooperative Extension)

The Blue Ridge and surrounding Western North Carolina mountains are real American black bear habitat; treat bear presence with a conservation tone, tracks-and-signs only, never as a threat or a mascot stunt (source: general Blue Ridge wildlife knowledge -- honor conservation framing)
